item: Extraction lock at 2 CPUs: occupancy over the four measured passes, its cost, and the cause of the unlocked slowdown isolated
summary: Collectors 2/4/8/14, 8 KB and 64 KB bodies, lock on and off, encrypted store with custody, 300 ms fetch latency, four measured passes of 720 articles per cell: the lock is held 9-25 % of the wall time with 8 KB bodies and 16-64 % with 64 KB bodies, a worker at 14 collectors waits 0.1 s / 0.78 s on average (longest 0.7 s / 10.9 s), and the lock costs no throughput beyond a run-to-run spread of up to 12 % (one cell 24 %). Cause of the unlocked slowdown measured: CPU not waiting, reproduces with a loop of os.stat calls and no lxml, needs no shared parser or XPath object, allocator not supported; the GIL hand-off mechanism is inferred and the XPath share of extract_article is not isolated. A first matrix read the per-pass lock statistics once and covered one pass of four; withdrawn and rerun, with a holds == stored check in the harness.
